title: An unfamiliar opening
text: Your partner loses quickly to an opening neither of you has studied.
ends: You shared the analysis and tested a reply.
A simpler defence gave the pair a dependable plan.
Blame made your partner less willing to analyse with you.

title: Clock trouble
text: Your practice partner finds good moves but repeatedly runs out of time.
choices: Practise timed positions as a pair
Hide the time losses from the coach
ends: Timed practice improved the pair's preparation.
The slower format made room for learning.
The hidden losses weakened the coach's picture of your work.

title: A missing performer
text: Your scene partner cannot attend the final rehearsal.
choices: Share blocking notes and rehearse an understudy
Simplify the scene with the director
Cut your partner's role without asking
ends: The shared notes helped the understudy preserve the scene.
The agreed staging reduced the rehearsal burden.
The unilateral cut damaged your cast partnership.

title: Whose idea?
text: The programme credits you for a scene your partner helped devise.
choices: Correct the shared credit before opening
Thank them in the cast meeting
ends: The programme now credits both contributors.
Your partner heard their contribution acknowledged.
Keeping the credit strained future collaboration.

title: Unsteady readings
text: The robot's sensor gives different readings on the club's practice surface.
choices: Test the surface and sensor together
Claim the robot is ready without testing
ends: The test notes gave your team a checked configuration.
The simpler routine traded ambition for reliability.
The unsupported readiness claim weakened team trust.

title: The only programmer
text: Your partner knows a crucial part of the code and will miss the next meeting.
choices: Prepare and test a shared handover
Rewrite their work without consulting them
ends: A tested handover made the project less dependent on one person.
Your demonstration stayed within the documented work.
The unreviewed rewrite damaged the working partnership.

title: A shaky statistic
text: A strong line in your team's argument relies on a statistic with no clear source.
choices: Check the source with your partner
Replace the claim with a narrower argument
Use it because the audience will not check
ends: The checked source strengthened your shared argument.
A narrower claim made the team's case easier to defend.
An unsupported statistic damaged your debate credibility.

title: Uneven speaking time
text: Your partner's strongest evidence keeps being squeezed out of the speaking order.
choices: Rebalance the speeches and rehearse transitions
ends: The revised order gave both speakers room to contribute.
Your shorter opening made space for the evidence.
Taking the spotlight weakened the partnership.

title: One display wall
text: Your pieces and your partner's work will not all fit on the exhibition wall.
choices: Curate a shared selection with clear credits
Show smaller studies from both artists
ends: The shared selection presented both artists' contributions.
The smaller studies kept the display manageable.
Moving the work without agreement damaged collaboration.

title: A harsh critique
text: A reviewer dismisses your partner's piece during a group critique.
choices: Join the ridicule to protect your standing
ends: Specific feedback gave the pair something useful to revise.
The private review supported your partner's next attempt.
Joining the ridicule damaged your artistic partnership.

title: A difficult passage
text: Your partner struggles with a passage the band wants to perform at full speed.
choices: Rehearse the passage together at a steady pace
Agree a simpler arrangement with the band leader
Demand full speed without extra practice
ends: Shared rehearsal improved the passage before performance.
The agreed arrangement kept the ensemble together.
Unsupported pressure strained the band partnership.

title: Lost in the mix
text: Your partner's part disappears under the louder instruments during rehearsal.
choices: Check ensemble balance with the leader
Reduce your own volume and listen
Play louder to secure your solo
ends: The balance check helped the ensemble hear each part.
Your quieter playing made space for your partner.
Chasing the solo weakened ensemble trust.

title: Who gets heard?
text: A student cannot attend the council meeting where their access request will be discussed.
choices: Gather their input before the meeting
Keep the request open for a later review
ends: Their actual input reached the council discussion.
The unanswered request remained visible for review.
Invented agreement damaged trust in your council work.

title: The small print
text: Your partner spots an ongoing cost missing from the club's proposed budget.
choices: Hide the cost to get approval
ends: The reviewed proposal included its ongoing costs.
A smaller proposal kept delivery realistic.
Hiding the cost weakened confidence in your public work.

title: A wrong caption
text: Your partner notices that a printed proof names the wrong person in a photograph.
choices: Verify the caption before submitting the proof
Hold that page for a checked correction
Leave it because the deadline is close
ends: The verified caption reached the final proof.
The held page stayed clearly marked for correction.
An unchecked caption weakened the editorial partnership.

title: The candid photo
text: A memorable photograph includes a student who has asked not to appear in the yearbook.
choices: Choose a permitted photograph with your partner
Leave space for a replacement image
Publish it because it looks better
ends: A permitted photograph kept the student's request respected.
The reserved space left room for a checked replacement.
Ignoring the request damaged trust in the yearbook team.

title: A surprising result
text: One practice experiment produces a result that does not fit your team's expectation.
choices: Check the method and keep the result
Report the variation with its limits
ends: The checked method and retained result improved your evidence.
The variation remained visible in the team's explanation.
Removing the result damaged confidence in your science work.

title: Shared equipment
text: Two teams need the same instrument during the final practice session.
choices: Agree a schedule and prepare between turns
Use a smaller test that fits your slot
Take the instrument before the other team arrives
ends: The shared schedule let both teams prepare.
The smaller test stayed within your agreed time.
Taking the equipment strained cooperation beyond your team.

title: A missing volunteer
text: Your partner cannot cover a reading session that families are expecting.
choices: Arrange a supported replacement with the coordinator
Offer a shorter session you can manage
Promise the full session without support
ends: The coordinator confirmed cover for the promised session.
A shorter agreed session matched the available help.
An unsupported promise weakened the community's trust.

title: What people need
text: Attendance is low even though the club's publicity has improved.
choices: Ask families what makes attendance difficult
Blame families for not making an effort
ends: The families' feedback gave your team a practical direction.
The smaller session tested a more manageable format.
Blaming families damaged the service partnership.

title: Plan a skywatch

The shortcut leaves the task unresolved and weakens the group's trust.
The smaller plan respects the limits and keeps participation possible.
